scope: Independent visual review of two native Unreal captures from the same saved camera, plus read-only image metrics and importer wiring inspection. No editor calls or asset changes.

visual_findings.finding: Broad violet bands and bright strand coverage change visibly along the middle/lower ring arc, while adjacent stone/gold geometry stays aligned. The change occupies broad regions, rather than only noisy edges.

Internal pale/blue streak and highlight patterns differ between captures across the upper/middle and lower fall. The island silhouette stays aligned. The pair supports changing water appearance; it does not independently establish downward velocity or a complete looping cycle.

temporal_noise_check.method: Compare corresponding RGB pixels, then repeat after a2px Gaussian blur to suppress high-frequency temporal-antialiasing noise. Compare effect regions with stable temple/cliff/gold/sky controls. No image files are modified.
temporal_noise_check.interpretation: Effect differences remain about8.6–18.5levels after blur; controls remain about0.16–0.43. This is substantially beyond the measured static-region TAA/noise baseline. It supports broad effect changes, not exact optical flow or shader pass isolation.

source_wiring.water_flow_axis_basis: Source Waterfall shader animates U; source waterfall mesh has U along stream length/vertical direction and V across width (water-source-axis-audit.json).
source_wiring.native_graph_evidence: effects-native-graphs.json enumerates Time/Panner nodes for native families, but may include deleted/orphaned expression objects. Node counts are not treated as connected-node counts.

limitations: Two still captures do not establish motion direction, speed, smoothness, seam-free wrap, or a fully observed repeat period.
File timestamp separation is wall-clock time, not recorded material simulation time.
This is a native UV-panner approximation, not a verified reconstruction of the original CryEngine procedural waterfall/energy simulation.
The comparison is not a controlled render-pass isolation test; low-frequency temporal lighting/translucency variation cannot be wholly excluded.
Water remains more pale/veined and energy more saturated than the supplied reference target.
